items.title_orig: 🎸 Se você pudesse escolher APENAS UMA década para ouvir rock pelo resto da vida, qual seria?
items.article_text:
Imagina a seguinte situação:
 Você só pode ouvir rock de uma única década pelo resto da vida.
 Depois de escolher, você nunca mais pode ouvir músicas de nenhuma outra década.
 Qual você escolheria?
 Anos 50 — Chuck Berry, Elvis, Little Richard, Buddy Holly...
 Anos 60 — Beatles, Stones, Hendrix, The Who, Cream...
 Anos 70 — Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, Black Sabbath, Queen, Deep Purple...
 Anos 80 — Metallica, Iron Maiden, The Cure, Guns N' Roses, Sonic Youth...
 Anos 90 — Nirvana, Alice in Chains, Soundgarden, Radiohead, Pearl Jam, Smashing Pumpkins...
 Anos 2000 — Linkin Park, System of a Down, White Stripes, Queens of the Stone Age, Arctic Monkeys, Muse...
 E não vale escolher pensando só na sua banda favorita.
 A pergunta é: qual década tem o melhor conjunto de rock para você viver ouvind

items.title_orig: Watch Eddie Vedder Busk in Dublin in Honor of Glen Hansard
items.article_text:
Eddie Vedder paid tribute to Glen Hansard by busking on Dublin’s Grafton Street, where the late musician got his start. Following Hansard’s funeral last week, Vedder showcased Pearl Jam‘s “Black” and Bruce Springsteen‘s “Drive All Night” on guitar alongside a group of fellow musicians on the local thoroughfare.

The clips were shared by Scottish musician Murdo Mitchell alongside photos taken by music photographer Danny Clinch. Mitchell and Hansard had a long friendship after Hansard spotted him busking at age 14 and invited him onstage at a show.

“After Glen’s funeral, I asked Dylan, Tom & Felix, if they would be up for a busk at Glen’s spot on Grafton St,” he wrote on Instagram. “They were more than keen so we rallied a group of some friends & we headed down even though it was like 3am, it felt like the right thing to do. His spirit was there. Not got much footage of it. We only had my guitar, a broken string & some heart, but we made it work.”

Vedder performed Hansard’s “The Song of Good Hope” at his funeral with Hansard’s Once collaborator Markéta Irglová and members of the Frames. During the memorial, Bono played a musical voicemail from Patti Smith before reciting reworked lyrics to U2 “Beautiful Day.” Both singers joined a group performance of Bob Dylan’s “Forever Young.”

Bono’s tribute also celebrated Hansard’s gift for friendship. “How do you do that?” he asked. “People on the green outside, best friends. People tuning in, best friends. Even people who haven’t met him, best friends. Everyone who met him, they just remember the day they met him.”

Hansard died July 29 at the age of 56 after a motorcycle crash. His death has led to an outpouring of grief from both his peers and his global audience.

items.title_orig: Eddie Vedder pays tribute to friend Glen Hansard by busking in his spot in Dublin city centre
items.article_text:
Hansard began his career busking on Grafton Street at the age of 13

Pearl Jam‘s Eddie Vedder has paid tribute to Glen Hansard by busking in his spot in Dublin’s city centre.

Hansard, known as the frontman of The Frames and one half of the duo The Swell Season, tragically died in a motorcycle crash last month. He was 56 years old.

The late musician and Oscar winning actor began his career busking on Grafton Street at the age of 13.

In tribute to his friend, Vedder recently busked in the same spot with local musicians after attending Hansard’s funeral at St. Patrick’s Cathedral.

During his short session the Pearl Jam frontman played his band’s classic track ‘Black’ and Bruce Springsteen‘s ‘Drive All Night’ on Hansard’s guitar. You can view footage below.

Murdo Mitchell just shared two beautiful videos of Eddie Vedder busking at Glen Hansard’s usual spot in Dublin, surrounded by Glen’s family and friends. No stage, no production — just music. pic.twitter.com/RejbqOqGo3

— pearljamonline.it (@pearljamonline) August 8, 2026

Eddie Vedder busking where Glen Hansard use to play.😢 pic.twitter.com/F5Szfxztmk

— Silvina (@silvina_176) August 8, 2026

Earlier, Vedder also performed at Hansard’s funeral with longtime collaborator Markéta Irglová and members of The Frames for a performance of ‘The Song of Good Hope’ in tribute to the late musician.

U2 frontman Bono also performed a spoken word version of ‘Beautiful Day’ at the service, reworking some of the lyrics to pay homage to him.
